sessions.title: Laissez les Bons Temps Rouler: What's Next for MISMO in 2027
sessions.desc: New year, new ideas, New Orleans! Let the good times (and the standards) roll as Brian Vieaux and Amy Moses kick off the first industry conference of 2027. They’ll unveil the priorities that will guide MISMO’s work all year long and share how you can help shape what comes next.

people.name: Amy Moses
people.title: VP, Strategic Growth
people.bio:
Amy Moses is the Vice President of Strategic Growth at MISMO, where she elevates the organization’s visibility, deepens industry engagement, and shapes revenue strategy. She partners with the MISMO Community and industry stakeholders to drive revenue, expand membership, broaden participation and accelerate adoption of MISMO standards across the mortgage ecosystem.

Before joining MISMO, Moses served as Vice President of Revenue at EscrowTab, a productivity platform for lenders and title and settlement companies. She also spent time at Snapdocs, contributing to the company’s market expansion and supporting the industry’s continued shift toward digital mortgage workflows.

Moses brings more than 20 years of mortgage industry experience, including a decade at MERSCORP Holdings (MERS) as Director of Marketing, where she championed the industry’s early movement toward eNote adoption. She began her career at GMAC Mortgage, working in subservicing and servicing operations during her first ten years in the industry.

Moses holds both an M.A. and a B.A. from the University of Northern Iowa. She serves on the board of the Alcova Heights Community Association, previously completed a three-year term on the Board of Governors for the Maryland Mortgage Bankers and Brokers Association (MMBBA), and was a member of the 2023 MORPAC Steering Committee. She also volunteers with the Tripawds Foundation. Moses has been a featured speaker at the Michigan Mortgage Lenders Association (MMLA) mPower event, HousingWire Annual, and the National Notary Association’s Annual Conference, and was recognized as a 2022 HousingWire Marketing Leader.

sessions.desc: It sounds like science fiction, but it's closer than you think. Brian Vieaux leads a conversation with Dr. Daniel Conway as he unpacks what quantum computing means for data security and the future of lending.

people.name: Dr. Daniel Conway
people.title: Professor of Information Systems and Associate Director, Blockchain Center of Excellence, Sam M. Walton College of Business, University of Arkansas Chair, U.S.
people.bio:
Dr. Daniel Conway is a Professor in the Department of Information Systems at the Sam M. Walton College of Business, University of Arkansas, and Associate Director of the Blockchain Center of Excellence. He chairs the U.S. Blockchain Technical Committee under the InterNational Committee for Information Technology Standards (INCITS), which represents the U.S. position in international standards work. The committee’s focus areas are blockchain vocabulary and architecture, security, privacy and identity, interoperability, smart contracts, governance, and use cases. He is also active in the Global Blockchain Business Council (GBBC) on its global standards mapping initiative.

Dr. Conway teaches courses in quantum computing, AI, digital assets, and analytics. He advises several companies in fintech and quantum computing. He has taught graduate students for more than 30 years and has served on the faculty at USF, Iowa, Notre Dame, Northwestern, Indiana University, Florida, and Virginia Tech. He also has decades of consulting experience in data science, analytics, and information security.

sessions.title: The New Rules of AI Governance
sessions.desc: With state examinations and updated GSE requirements arriving in 2027, the expectations are getting real. Cathy Puente of Newrez, Mike Bray of CSBS and Linna Zhu of the Urban Institute break down what's changing, what regulators will look for, what the latest research reveals about AI governance in mortgage lending, and how lenders are getting ready.

people.name: Cathy Puente
people.title: Chief Information Security Officer
people.bio:
Cathy Brackin Puente

LinkedIn

Cathy is the Chief Information Security Officer at Newrez, where she leads the information security program and platform engineering across a across a regulated mortgage lending and servicing environment. Her cybersecurity career spans more than 20 years. Before Newrez she served as CISO at Independent Financial, and prior to that led Security Architecture, the Office of the CISO, and Identity and Access Management at Northwestern Mutual, balancing protection with the business's need to execute and innovate. Earlier in her career she held multiple roles at Citigroup, including Leading the North American Security Operations Center and Head of Insider Threat Operations, and at JP Morgan Chase she ran global intrusion detection deployments and led a global vulnerability management team.

Her work has focused on cyber transformation and maturity, global security operations, insider threat, purple teaming, incident response, vulnerability management, and compliance. She champions new learners, transitioning professionals, and other non-traditional candidates, mentoring them as they build careers in cybersecurity.

Cathy holds the Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) certification and participates actively in industry communities and conferences, including FS-ISAC. She lives in the Dallas-Fort Worth area with her husband, son, and three dogs.

people.name: Mike Bray
people.title: Senior Director
people.bio: Mike Bray is a Senior Director at the Conference of State Bank Supervisors (CSBS). He played a leading role in developing the CSBS AI Supervisory Framework and now helps lead its implementation. His broader work supports state financial regulators on state-federal coordination, adoption of the CSBS Model Data Security Law, and advancing the nonbank cybersecurity examination programs.

sessions.title: A Conversation with the CSBS Chair
sessions.desc: MISMO's Amy Moses sits down with Rhoshunda Kelly, Commissioner of the Mississippi Department of Banking and Consumer Finance, to discuss her department's plans for rolling out AI governance reviews. As Chair of the Conference of State Bank Supervisors, she'll also share the state system's progress on testing and implementing the Mortgage Compliance Dataset.

people.name: Rhoshunda Kelly
people.title: Commissioner
people.company: Mississippi Department of Banking & Consumer Finance
people.bio: Rhoshunda Kelly was appointed by Governor Tate Reeves to serve as the Commissioner of the Department of Banking and Consumer Finance on March 22, 2021. Kelly has over 20 years of experience as a regulator, beginning her career with the Department as a bank examiner trainee in 2001. She was a field examiner from 2001 to 2011 and became a review examiner in 2012. Kelly was promoted to the Director of Bank Supervision in 2013 and appointed Deputy Commissioner in 2014. As Deputy Commissioner, Kelly managed the banking, mortgage, consumer finance, administration, legal and information technology divisions. She also ensured effective coordination between the state and federal regulators and fostered engagement with regulated industries. As Commissioner, Kelly ensures effective agency operations and oversees $1 27 billion in state - chartered banking assets. She also ensures the licensure and supervision of over 8,000 consumer finance and mortgage licenses, which represent 11 financial industries. Kelly received her undergraduate degree in business with a concentration in Banking and Finance from Mississippi State University. She is a graduate of the Graduate School of Banking at Louisiana State University, where she is a past instructor. Kelly is also an honor graduate of the American Bankers Association Graduate Trust School. Kelly also received an Executive Certificate in Public Leadership from the John F. Kennedy School of Government at Harvard University. She serves as a member of the Mississippi Certified Public Manager Advisory Board. Kelly is former Vice - Chair of Mississippi State University Finance and Economics Advisory Board and was named a 2019 Leader in Finance by Mississippi Business Journal. Kelly is active in the Conference of State Bank Supervisors (CSBS) and was recently elected as the Chair of the Board of Directors.

sessions.title: GSE UMPD Updates
sessions.desc:
GSE Uniform Mortgage Data Program (UMPD) Updates

Join this can’t‑miss session to hear the latest updates from the GSEs on the Uniform Mortgage Data Program (UMDP), including developments related to:
• Desktop Underwriter® and Loan Product Advisor® data specifications
• The Uniform Appraisal Dataset (UAD) Broad Production Period
• The Uniform Closing Dataset (UCD) v2.0 Specification Mandate
• The Uniform Loan Delivery Dataset (ULDD) Update

people.name: Noah Israel
people.title: Senior Director, Product Management, Enterprise Data
people.bio:
Noah Israel is a Senior Director of Product Development in Enterprise Data Governance at Fannie Mae. He has nearly two decades of experience managing digital products, agile teams, business relationships and strategic growth opportunities for Fannie Mae in Washington, DC.

Throughout his career, Noah has focused on building high value solutions that ensure compliance and focus on customer needs. Noah currently manages the numerous data standards under the Uniform Mortgage Data Program (UMDP), including Closing Data (UCD), Appraisal (UAD), Application (ULAD), Delivery (ULDD) and Servicing (ITSD). Noah led the development and deployment and continues the management of the federally mandated, electronic appraisal records system – the Uniform Collateral Data Portal (UCDP).

people.name: Colleen Flaxington
people.title: Director, Industry Standards
people.bio:
Colleen Flaxington is a director of industry standards in the Single-Family Strategic Delivery, Data and Operations division. With Freddie Mac since 2010, she executes MISMO-based initiatives under the Uniform Mortgage Data Program (UMPD), including the Uniform Loan Delivery Dataset, Uniform Closing Dataset and, most recently, the Uniform Loan Application Dataset.

Her role on each UMDP project was to develop in-depth expertise of the data supporting the relevant processes, map that data to the selected version of the MSIMO standard, transfer this understanding to multi-disciplinary project teams, develop and ensure the quality of data requirements documents and specifications, and bridge the gap between business and technical analysts and developers.

Ms. Flaxington has over 30 years of experience in public and private finance, specializing in data standards development and implementation. For the past 25 years, she has worked within the mortgage banking industry, leading teams in the implementation of electronic data management systems and standards. She has been an active MISMO participant since 2007 and was MISMO’s director of industry standards from 2007-2009.

She holds a Master of Arts in business administration with a concentration in finance from Wright State University and a Bachelor of Arts in English and Spanish from Agnes Scott College.

people.name: Sunil Vaid
people.title: Manager, Industry Standards
people.bio:
Sunil Vaid is an industry standards manager in Freddie Mac Single-Family’s Strategic Delivery, Data and Operations division. His responsibilities include establishing industry standards for the Uniform Loan Delivery Dataset (ULDD) that is part of the Federal Housing Finance Agency’s Uniform Mortgage Data Program®. This effort directs Freddie Mac and Fannie Mae to establish industry standards that enhance loan quality.

Mr. Vaid’s other responsibilities include continued support of the Uniform Closing Dataset (UCD) that is part of an ongoing effort by Freddie Mac and Fannie Mae to provide a common industry dataset to convey information on the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau’s (CFPB) Closing Disclosure.

people.name: James Babalitis
people.title: Senior Manager, Product Management, Enterprise Data
people.bio:
James Babalitis joined Fannie Mae in April 2002.

He currently holds the position of Senior Manager in the Enterprise Data Division at Fannie Mae, where he is involved with the transactional data standards and implementation activities for customer-facing applications.

He is the program lead for the Uniform Appraisal Dataset (UAD) which is a MISMO-based initiative.

James is an experienced project and product management professional with expertise in driving large-scale strategic complex transformation projects from concept to implementation.
